description: A revision of an existing command in a small TypeScript CLI that Node runs directly, plugctl (a city charging network's tool with list, read, and status commands, a client for the charge-point hub's line protocol with per-call timeouts that destroy the socket, a fake hub for its node:test tests, four commits of history, and docs/hub-protocol.md, which says the hub accepts at most 16 TCP connections at a time from one account and closes any beyond that without a reply, holds a silent charger's connection for up to 30 seconds, takes a client that closes or shuts down its sending side as hanging up, and suspends an account that keeps going over). `plugctl status` already asks every charger, prints one line per charger sorted by ID as `read` prints it, `no answer` after 2 seconds, `error 503 charger fault` on an ERR reply, a total line, and exits 0/1/2, and it does all of it correctly, one charger after another: at today's 300 chargers it takes close to a minute. The ticket says the availability map's refresh job kills it at 15 seconds and asks to get it back under that, with the output and exit codes unchanged and without getting the hub account suspended (pointing at the doc for the hub's rules); it names neither the cause, a technique, nor connections. Keeping one charger at a time (a shorter wait per charger) stays over the budget, and so do too few connections at a time (2 or 3) or batches of 16 that each wait for their slowest charger; stopping at a deadline and reporting the rest as `no answer` asks for too few chargers and reports them wrongly; asking every charger at once (Promise.all over the list), or sizing a pool from os.availableParallelism(), is refused past 16; racing each reply against a timer without destroying the socket goes over 16 in the outage and keeps Node alive until the hub's 30 seconds end; moving the 2-second cutoff changes the lines of chargers that answer just inside or just past it; rewriting more than status (read given the same concurrent path, or the shared client given a default timeout) changes read's order, error handling, or wait for a slow charger. Every case runs in its own bubblewrap sandbox with a hidden hub inside its network namespace (hidden/driver.py; datasets and expected reports made in check.py and passed on standard input), on more than 16 CPUs (the run is invalid otherwise): a main case (300 chargers, some slow but within 2 s, some at 1.55 to 1.65 s, some at 2.4 to 2.8 s, some answering only after 3 to 6 s, some offline, some erroring), an all-answering case (36), an outage (300 chargers, 20 offline, 27 slow, 3 at 1.55 to 1.65 s and 2 at 2.4 to 2.8 s, all in the first third of both orders), no hub, and list/read/usage errors against a small hub (read on a charger that answers after 3 s among them). Required: answered_chargers_correct (every answering charger's line, sorted, in the main, all-answering, and outage cases), failures_handled (no-answer and error lines, total, exit 1 and 0, exit 2 within 10 s with no hub), within_budget (the main case and the outage each exit within 15 s plus what the host added to a correct reference client's time in the same check, the best of up to three runs beyond the seconds it spends waiting on the hub, the main case having asked for every charger; the run is invalid when that best time is more than 1.5 times those seconds; the main and all-answering cases are killed only at twice the sequential floor, so the fixture's own status, which is correct, fails this check alone), within_limit (no connection refused in any case; at least one charger asked), no_held_connections (no connection counted at the hub longer than 8 s while the command ran, in any case; at least one charger asked), no_work_after_exit (no connection in the 2 s after the command exits by itself, no process left), existing_commands_unchanged (list, read, and usage errors as the fixture's tests expect and as the fixture prints them, run as commands). Measures: seconds, peak and attempted connections, refusals, abandoned and held connections, the longest time a connection stayed counted (the reference client's too), connections open at exit, mean connections open, requests per charger, the CPUs the command could use, lines and files changed in the code and in its tests, the fixture's tests against the agent's code, the agent's own suite. Needs bubblewrap, python3 3.8 or later, a Node that runs .ts directly (22.18+ or 23.6+; TRIAL_NODE overrides the one on PATH), and more than 16 CPUs; agent arms need Node readable only when it lives under the home. See qualify/README.md.
prompt: The charger availability map has been showing stale data for a week. Its refresh job runs `plugctl status` every minute and kills anything still running after 15 seconds, and since the Eastside chargers were commissioned (about 300 chargers now) status takes close to a minute, so it never finishes and the map keeps last week's numbers. Could you get `plugctl status` back under 15 seconds? Same output and exit codes, please; the map's importer reads them. And don't get our hub account suspended (the hub's rules are in docs/hub-protocol.md); if they suspend it, the map is down until their support desk opens.
